newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmaker seeks tobacco tax hike for budget.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmaker seeks tobacco tax hike for budget.

text.p: A California lawmaker said on Wednesday he would introduce a bill to raise the state's cigarette tax by 80 cents a pack to help ease California's budget crunch.
The proposal by Assemblyman Tom Torlakson, a Democrat, would raise the state's tobacco tax from 37 cents a pack to $1.17 a pack, raising $1.2 billion a year for the state.
The assemblyman said his measure would, if approved, offset the state's $1.2 billion payment to the California Public Employees' Retirement System (Calpers).

A state appeals court ruled earlier this year that the governor and the legislature improperly withheld the money from Calpers in the early 1990s to balance state budgets during California's deepest economic downturn since the Depression. The state Supreme Court let the ruling stand.
This week, Gov. Pete Wilson ordered the state to immediately repay Calpers. The state controller transferred the money to the pension system late on Wednesday.
Lawmakers fear the payment will force them to sharply curtail their spending plans for the 1997-1998 budget year. Funding for tax cuts and other programs may cut, they said.
Torlakson said his tobacco tax measure would replenish state revenues.
"It (the tax measure) allows us to provide health care coverage for children and fund other high priority programs," he said. "This budget-balancer makes complete sense."
Assemblyman Kevin Shelley, who chairs the Assembly Democratic caucus, said the tobacco tax proposal had the support of a majority of Democrats in the Assembly.
